tasks.spec:
You are a build worker writing a scripted-conversation timing driver. OFFLINE while building: no network calls, no git, no MCP, no skills; write only in your working directory. The script will be EXECUTED LATER by separate runner tasks with credentials in env.

PURPOSE: measure per-turn latency, per-turn message count, and node routing of a Bland conversational pathway version, so two versions (or two node models) can be compared on identical scripted turns. Today the harness records none of this.

REFERENCE (read for proven mechanics, then adapt; never modify): /home/ankit114/repos/mott-v21-snap/harness/pathway_harness.py - chat mechanics: API base https://api.bland.ai, PATHWAY_ID 94abad8b-fbe2-4e67-9c64-d9b586dd2653, per-turn POST /v1/pathway/chat/{chat_id} with pathway_id/pathway_version/request_data; responses carry assistant_responses (list), current_node_id, variables. Also /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/checks/failure_mode_run.py for chat-session setup and masking style.

WRITE ./turn_timer.py, usage: turn_timer.py <pathway_version> <script.json> <label>. script.json is {"turns": ["hi", "..."]}. VALIDATION ORDER IS A CONTRACT: (1) parse args, (2) load script.json, (3) if any turn, stripped and lowercased, equals '1' or 'yes' print the refusal reason and exit 2 BEFORE any network call or env read - this driver must never book, (4) require env BLAND_API_KEY else exit 1. Then open a fresh chat on the given version and send each turn in order. Per turn print EXACTLY one line: TURN=<i> WALL_MS=<int> N_MSGS=<count of assistant messages this turn> NODE=<current_node_id> SAID=<assistant messages joined with ' | ', digit runs of 5+ masked to last 4, truncated at 200 chars>. WALL_MS is monotonic wall time around the HTTP round-trip. After the last turn print: RESULT label=<label> turns=<n> total_wall_ms=<int> filler_hits=<count of assistant messages across the whole run containing the phrase 'one moment while i check' case-insensitively>. Per-call HTTP timeout 180s; on any turn HTTP failure print TURN_FAIL turn=<i> reason=<...> and exit 1.

VERIFY before finishing: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile turn_timer.py passes; no-args run exits nonzero printing usage; a script containing a 'yes' turn exits 2 without needing BLAND_API_KEY. Final message <=15 lines.
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile turn_timer.py || exit 1; if python3 turn_timer.py >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'CHECK FAILED: no-args run must exit nonzero with usage'; exit 1; fi; printf '{"turns":["hi","yes"]}' > refuse_test.json; python3 turn_timer.py 92 refuse_test.json probe >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: booking-turn script must be refused with exit 2 before any network, got exit $rc"; exit 1; }; echo 'PASS: compiles; usage guard; booking refusal precedes network'
tasks.verified: A reusable per-turn timing driver for any pathway version: wall-clock, message count, node id, and filler-phrase count per scripted turn, structurally incapable of booking.

tasks.spec:
You are a build worker writing a latency-decomposition script for a real SMS conversation. OFFLINE while building: no network calls, no git, no MCP, no skills; write only in your working directory. The script will be EXECUTED LATER by a separate runner task with credentials in env.

PURPOSE: Ankit experienced ~40s answers on the Mott SMS booking line tonight; server-side turns measured 3-12s. Decompose the gap truthfully per turn using two record sources: (a) the Bland conversation's message records with their timestamps, (b) the gateway's CloudWatch logs. The suspected mechanism is Bland's two-message habit ('Let me check that for you' then the real answer = two LLM generations + two SMS sends) plus carrier delivery.

SOURCES: fetch conversation messages the same way the deployed gateway does - reuse the fetch code path from /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mott-raw-text/work2/raw-text-authority-v2/bland_gateway_live.py (read it; import from absolute path without triggering server entrypoints; it logs raw_fetch msgs= near line 944). Preserve every timestamp field the API returns. CloudWatch: log group /ecs/mott-booking-gateway, region us-east-1, via aws CLI subprocess or boto3 with ambient credentials, window from env WINDOW_START/WINDOW_END (ISO8601 UTC).

WRITE ./timing_report.py, usage: timing_report.py <conversation_id>. Env: BLAND_API_KEY, WINDOW_START, WINDOW_END. Output: (1) ./waterfall.csv, one row per patient turn: turn, patient_ts, gw_first_log_ts, gw_last_log_ts, agent_msg1_ts, agent_msg2_ts, gap_patient_to_msg1_s, gap_msg1_to_msg2_s, msg_class (filler+answer | single-answer | no-reply). (2) stdout machine lines: one 'WATERFALL turn=<i> gap_to_first=<s> gap_between=<s|NA> class=<...>' per row; 'TWO_MSG_TURNS=<n>/<total>'; 'SUMMARY median_reply_s=<s> p95_reply_s=<s>'; and for any segment the records cannot measure print 'UNMEASURED: <segment> - not present in any record' (carrier delivery to handset is expected to be one). If message timestamps lack sub-minute precision or any needed field is absent, print the limitation explicitly - never interpolate invented times. Mask digit runs of 5+ to last 4 in any printed message text. Per-call timeout 120s; fetch failure prints why, exits 1.

VERIFY before finishing: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile timing_report.py passes; no-args run exits nonzero printing usage. Final message <=15 lines.
